evidence: Single package ('postgresql_metrics') containing all core logic — no separate service boundaries or deployment units
Clear modularity with domain-separated modules (e.g., metrics_gatherer, postgres_queries, prepare_db, metrics_logic)
High cohesion within modules (e.g., metrics_gatherer aggregates gather functions for each metric, postgres_queries encapsulates all DB access)
Dependencies flow from higher-level modules (metrics_logic) to lower-level modules (common, postgres_queries) without visible inversion of control or formal ports/adapters pattern
No explicit adapters, drivers, or domain core separation (ruling out hexagonal)
No strict layers (e.g., presentation/business/data access) — logic and data access are interleaved (e.g., postgres_queries contains both querying and parsing logic)
Entry point is a main() function in metrics_logic — typical of monolithic CLI tools
Repository depth is shallow (max depth=2), no complex hierarchical subsystems
FAN_OUT is low (~2.2), indicating loosely coupled modules without heavy cross-dependencies
risks: As the system evolves, tight coupling between modules (e.g., metrics_gatherer imports all metric-specific and DB-specific functions) may hinder testability
Mixing SQL queries, parsing, and stateful logic in postgres_queries may lead to违反 separation of concerns
Lack of formal dependency boundaries could increase maintenance cost over time
Metrics gatherer's monolithic import list suggests potential violation of Single Responsibility and Interface Segregation Principles
